indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of the population whose wastewater is collected and treated in urban wastewater treatment plants, expressed as a percentage. It covers at least secondary (biological) treatment. Data are reported by member states under the Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive and compiled by Eurostat.
rationale: Access to adequate wastewater treatment is fundamental for protecting water quality and public health. Untreated wastewater contaminates rivers, lakes and coastal waters. Progress means an increasing proportion of the population connected to at least secondary wastewater treatment.
methodology_characteristics: Data are reported by member states every two years under Council Directive 91/271/EEC concerning urban wastewater treatment. The indicator covers agglomerations generating more than 2,000 population equivalents. Eurostat compiles and publishes the data as a percentage of the total population.
indicator_name: Population connected to urban wastewater treatment
